actuallyOpenedImages.scope: Full original; all four quadrant groups viewed. No browser, game view, crop PNG or native-size animation was opened.

loose.observed: Sparse horizontal ash-gray winged insects with large clear spaces. Natural variation of paired wing angle and body heading is visible among the larger readable insects.
limits: Not a complete per-insect anatomy audit; the smallest marks do not resolve appendages.
No looping flight or hovering transitions demonstrated.

dense.observed: Dense oval colony with many overlapping ash-gray moth silhouettes and a central less-occupied area. No lamp/torch/flame or game tile is drawn.
limits: Overlapping wing/body shapes cannot be converted reliably to a literal insect count.
Central opening and nearby background contain low-alpha remnants, so not a mathematically empty aperture.
Larger moths visually resemble detailed moth/butterfly silhouettes; small-scale species legibility remains for actual integration.

moving.observed: Wide asymmetric horizontal swarm, with a compact group at the right and smaller/sparser marks toward the left. Different individuals have different wing openings.
limits: This is one static directional distribution. It does not prove actual individual rightward flight or a coherent wingbeat phase sequence.

dispersing.observed: Widely separated ash-gray insects around a more open middle; multiple outward body headings. No attack/explosion/blood is painted.
limits: This is not a temporal correspondence to the other states; individuals are not tracked between panels.

notes: The image viewer displays substantial RGB gray fields, including behind alpha=0 pixels; this is not an opaque black/gray rectangle. Numeric RGBA analysis is recorded separately.
There are actual low-alpha background remnants: wide vertical gutter alpha max1, horizontal max2; canvas edge305 pixels at alpha1. No alpha cleanup was performed.
All source alpha values are<=253: insects are near-opaque, not fully alpha255.
Textured wing detail and anti-aliased edge alpha are present; strict hard-edged pixel-grid consistency and game-scale readability were not accepted.
